title: Si/Al2O3 Dual-Cavity Filter with Band-Edge Constrained Optimization
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining band-edge layer thickness bounds to [450,620]nm while initializing from previous best candidate with ±4% perturbation will improve spectral transition sharpness and increase best_target_score by redirecting optimization budget from interior phase-trimming to edge sharpening.
design_principle: Dual-cavity defect filter with quarter-wave stack mirrors; band-edge layers control passband transitions while interior layers provide bulk phase matching.
proposed_topology: Air | [Si/Al2O3]×11 | CaF2 substrate; 22 finite layers total with dual-cavity defect structure: Mirror1(5 pairs)-Cavity1-Mirror2(4 pairs)-Cavity2-Mirror3(5 pairs)
design_variables: Layer thicknesses with differentiated bounds: layers 0-3 and 18-21 bounded [450,620]nm, layers 4-17 bounded [400,1100]nm
manufacturing_considerations: Si and Al2O3 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
Band-edge layer bounds reflect manufacturable tolerance window
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
Quarter-wave stack principle for high-reflectance mirrors
Defect cavity resonance for narrow passband transmission
expected_advantages: Narrower band-edge bounds focus optimization on transition regions
Initialization from previous best candidate reduces search space
±4% perturbation maintains exploration while respecting prior convergence
known_risks: Over-constraining band-edge layers may limit achievable transition sharpness
Local optimum from previous iteration may persist
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate with air incidence at normal incidence. Layer sequence: Si(511nm)/Al2O3(575nm)/Si(576nm)/Al2O3(591nm)/Si(514nm)/Al2O3(578nm)/Si(682nm)/Al2O3(432nm)/Si(493nm)/Al2O3(550nm)/Si(767nm)/Al2O3(452nm)/Si(449nm)/Al2O3(506nm)/Si(792nm)/Al2O3(463nm)/Si(503nm)/Al2O3(1069nm)/Si(737nm)/Al2O3(758nm)/Si(491nm)/Al2O3(655nm). Apply thickness bounds: layers 0-3 and 18-21 bounded [450,620]nm; layers 4-17 bounded [400,1100]nm. Initialize optimization from thickness vector [502.2,538.4,621.0,599.4,496.3,583.2,611.8,497.1,535.4,545.4,906.3,626.7,613.3,510.4,544.6,606.4,629.1,1016.8,461.4,449.6,575.7,865.4]nm with ±4% Gaussian perturbation. Optimize for mean transmittance in 3250-3350nm and 4200-4300nm bands (maximize) and mean transmittance in 2500-3100nm and 4450-5000nm bands (minimize). Use gradient-based thickness optimizer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive to constrain band-edge layer bounds [450,620]nm and initialize from previous best candidate with ±4% perturbation to focus optimization on spectral transition regions.
